summary: Hotel RFID projects usually hinge on three decisions: which credential format fits the guest journey, which chip family matches the lock estate, and how much personalization should happen before cards or wristbands reach the property.
Use these short answers to decide whether this page matches the project before moving into the detail.
Choose cards, wristbands or a mixed program based on guest flow and property type.

faq.question: When should a hotel keep cards instead of switching to wristbands?
faq.answer: Card-first programs still make sense for most room-key deployments, especially where guests expect a familiar form factor and amenity access is limited.

faq.question: Can hotels run cards and wristbands together?
faq.answer: Yes. Mixed programs are common when guest rooms use cards while pools, gyms or VIP amenities use wristbands.

faq.question: What speeds up a hotel RFID quote?
faq.answer: Sharing the current lock estate, chip requirement, preferred credential format and target sample quantity removes most early back-and-forth.
